# dsh-find-viewer

A find bar for the DeepSeek Harness sidebar's text preview, added to the document
toolbar the previe

w already has. It searches the file, shows the match count, highlights
the hits, and jumps between t

ready has. It searches the file, shows the match count, highlights
the hits, and jumps between them.
English | 中文
## What it does

- **A magnifier button in the document toolbar**, next to *Open in app*. It appears only
while the p

ane shows a text file, so PDF, image, HTML, spreadsheet and Office previews
keep their toolbar uncha

nged.
- **A find bar** with an input, `n/m` count, previous/next, match case (`Aa`), whole word
(`W`

/Ctrl+F`** opens it while the preview is the pane you last clicked in.
- **Search a selection**: sel

ect text in the preview, then open the bar — the selection
becomes the keyword. A multi-line selecti

on uses its first line; a selection longer than
200 characters is ignored.
- **Hits are highlighted

in the colours Edge and Chrome use for find-on-page**: yellow
`#FFFF00` for hits, orange `#FF9632` f

or the current one, black text on both. Typing a
keyword scrolls to the first hit.
## Match counts
| Preview | Counts | Jump | Highlight |
| Plain text, code | Whole file, exact | Any line, including lines the viewer has not loaded yet | E

very rendered hit |
| Markdown | The text currently rendered | Every rendered hit | Every rendered h

rendered hit |
| Markdown | The text currently rendered | Every rendered hit | Every rendered hit |

Markdown differs because the official Markdown view renders formatted HTML: source
markers are gone

and it exposes no per-line anchors, so a find bar over it can only count
and jump within what is ren

dered — the count grows as more of the document loads. Plain
text and code keep their source lines i
n the DOM, so those two count the whole file.

Files the bar covers: Markdown (`.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdx`), plain text and logs, and code
(`.js`, `

.ts`, `.py`, `.go`, `.rs`, `.java`, `.c`, `.cpp`, `.css`, `.json`, `.yaml`,
`.toml`, `.sh`, `.sql`,

and more). Spreadsheets (`.csv`, `.tsv`), HTML and SVG keep their
own previews. A file with no suffi

x, such as `Dockerfile`, is not covered, because the
viewer picks renderers by file suffix.

## How it works

The plugin has no build step and no runtime dependencies. Its browser half registers one
entry in th

e document toolbar's additive list slot
(`sidebar.right.tab.document.actions`), a slot that only app

ends, so no existing control is
replaced.

- Whole-file counting reads the file with the harness's own paged file Remote
(`remote.workspaceFile

s.read`), which is the same reader the preview itself uses.
- Highlights use the CSS Custom Highligh

t API: the bar registers ranges and never edits
the DOM the official renderers own.
- Jumping to a l

ine the viewer has not loaded yet asks the sidebar to navigate to that line
(`sidebarRight.openResou

rce`), which makes the viewer load the pages it needs.
- Locale lookups go through the client locale

service (English and Chinese dictionaries are
included).

It imports no harness client package as a module and registers no global keyboard handler;
`Cmd/Ctrl
+F` is only intercepted while the preview is the pane you last clicked in.
## Limits

- The whole-file scan covers the first 20,000 lines or 4 MiB, whichever comes first; the
find bar sa

ys so when a file is larger. Up to 3,000 hits are painted, and up to 50,000 are
counted (`50000+` be

yond that).
- Highlights need the CSS Custom Highlight API (Chromium 105+, Safari 17.2+, Firefox 140

+).
Where it is missing, counts and jumps still work and hits are not painted.
- Matches do not span

lines.
- Verified against DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0-rc.2`. The plugin declares no `engines.dsh`
range
because its compatibility with later versions has not been tested.
